clue.text: A restaurant with musicians by the water

parts.note: the brass is the section of an orchestra or band playing horns and trumpets
Erie is one of the Great Lakes, a body of water

explanation.surface: An eatery with a band playing beside the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the band next to the water. Lake ERIE is a North American Great Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eating place serving food and drink.

clue.text: Some Lutheran courageously showing resentment

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A brave Protestant reformer is nonetheless bitter about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is lasting bitterness or ill will, which is what resentment shows.

clue.text: Trying to interview the top man

parts.note: to see someone can mean to meet or interview them, as a manager sees a candidate
a king is the man at the very top of a realm

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to get an audience with the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking to do something means attempting or endeavouring to do it.

clue.text: Sine qua non in action

parts.note: a lawsuit, or legal action, cannot succeed without proof put before the court: that proof is its indispensable condition

explanation.surface: An essential condition being put into practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' looks like activity in general but means a lawsuit; 'sine qua non' is Latin for something without which a thing cannot be.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof laid before a court is the indispensable requirement of a legal case.

clue.text: Contestants take on so!

parts.note: the verb meaning take on or fight with is also the command given to fencers to cross blades and begin a bout

explanation.surface: An instruction telling competitors to tackle each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a verb for taking someone on and the call that starts competitors such as fencers fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to grips with an opponent is to enter into combat, and the same word is the order to begin.

clue.text: Constantly accommodating a demanding Oriental

indicators.note: accommodating means holding within, so one piece houses the others

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always or constantly
a stern taskmaster is demanding and strict

explanation.surface: A person from the Far East who is always making exacting demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constantly' gives the poetic contraction of 'ever'; 'demanding' wants to describe the Oriental but supplies the word for strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the Orient, the lands of the east, is a person from the east.

clue.text: Participants go and dance a certain figure

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Participants go and dance a certain figure', gives the anagram fodder GO AND but nothing supplies the remaining E and C of DECAGON; the clue appears garbled or cut short in the OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: Participants go and dance a certain figure

clue.text: Remain around the coach, as the law requires

indicators.note: around means the first word is wrapped about the second

parts.note: to stay is to remain where one is
a tutor is a private coach or teacher

explanation.surface: Someone stays near the trainer because regulations demand it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus but is a teacher here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something required by statute is mandated by legislation.

clue.text: Took meals in the home, being most fastidious

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside another here

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home, and by extension any snug home
ate is the past tense of eat, to take meals

explanation.surface: Someone had dinner at home and was very particular about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tidiest, most fussy person is the most particular about order.

clue.text: Finish up with mice maybe becoming prevalent in the area

parts.note: to finish up is to end, as in end up somewhere

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of mice might be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A place overrun with rodents becomes a hotbed of something local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish up' reads as a phrase about the mice, but it is the first piece; 'maybe' is the anagram signal on the rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease that is endemic is regularly found among the people of a particular region.

clue.text: Appeal to a sober person to hold transport back

indicators.note: hold means the first piece keeps the second clasped inside it

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a person who drinks no alcohol

indicators.note: back means the word for transport is read from right to left

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle for transport

explanation.surface: Trying to win over a non-drinker by having them keep a vehicle in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, for teetotal, is a standard label for a non-drinker; 'back' reverses only the transport word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract someone is to draw or allure them, much as appealing to them does.

clue.text: The long arm of the paw!

definitions.text: The long arm of the paw!

parts.words: The long arm of the paw!
parts.note: plays on the long arm of the law, the reach of the police, with paw making it a four-legged officer

explanation.surface: A twist on the saying about the far reach of law enforcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The long arm of the law' means the police's reach; swapping in 'paw' points to a canine member of the force.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog trained to help officers enforce the law is a four-legged agent of the force.

clue.text: Expresses disapproval of things

definitions.meaning: to protest against, as a lawyer does in court
items or articles, inanimate bits of matter

explanation.surface: Someone complains about items.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means protests against; as a plural noun it means physical items or articles.

clue.text: Maintains a bus tore off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone off course and been jumbled

explanation.surface: A coach went speeding away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'tore off' but signals rearranging A BUS TORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something out is to confirm or support it, which is what maintaining a claim does.

clue.text: Appalling sort of shirt and something to smoke brought back

parts.note: a T-shirt is a type of shirt, giving the letter T

indicators.note: brought back means the word for something to smoke is read in reverse

parts.note: a cigar is something one smokes

explanation.surface: A dreadful garment and a smoke returned to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of shirt' takes just the letter that names a T-shirt; 'brought back' reverses the smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadfully sad or calamitous is shocking, just as a disaster is.

clue.text: Court officials provide gifts for employees

parts.note: to tip is to give a small present of money for service
staffs are the bodies of workers employed by organisations

explanation.surface: Advice to hand out bonuses to the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a court officer, named after the metal-tipped staff once carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's or court attendant, an officer serving a judge.

clue.text: Decoration of golf club quite unpleasant

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club with a metal head
cross means bad-tempered, and so disagreeable in manner

explanation.surface: Ornament on a golf club that is rather nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Cross is a German military medal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Cross is a military medal for bravery, a kind of honour awarded to soldiers.

clue.text: Always to be in the right, that's the dream

indicators.note: in places one word within the letters of the others

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right
i.e. stands for id est, Latin for that is
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Being always correct is someone's fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in' sets the word for always between the right and the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, a state of absorbed musing.

clue.text: The dreamer gives some thought to a catalogue

parts.note: an idea is a thought or notion
a list is an itemised catalogue

explanation.surface: A visionary devotes attention to an index.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues perfect visions, often unrealistically, like a fantasist.

clue.text: Stick around a trainee using the phone

indicators.note: around means the first word goes about the others

parts.note: to cling is to stick fast
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Someone holds onto a novice during a telephone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps CLING round A and L; L for learner comes from British learner plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone means ringing them up on a telephone.

clue.text: Finding listening equipment in the drain can be chilling

indicators.note: in means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: to drain dishes or vegetables is to let them dry
the ear is the organ we hear with

explanation.surface: Discovering a hearing aid down the plughole could be unnerving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drain' looks like a noun but is the verb, to make dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreary is bleak and cheerless, giving a cold, depressing feel.

clue.text: Blow up when there's general chaos

indicators.note: chaos implies the letters of general are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A photograph is enlarged amid confusion among the top brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' could mean explode, but here it is to make a photograph bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a photograph is to make it bigger, to magnify it.

clue.text: A writer for children managed a few

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
some means a few or a certain number

explanation.surface: A children's author ran a small number of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ransome was an English author of sailing adventure books for young readers.

clue.text: Gnats tormented a worker still

indicators.note: tormented suggests the letters of gnats are twisted out of shape

parts.note: the worker ant is a classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Midges bothered an employee who kept motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tormented' rearranges GNATS into STAGN, then ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is motionless and not flowing.

clue.text: Prior occupying quarters in a French town

indicators.note: occupying means filling the space inside the other piece

parts.note: N and S are compass points, quarters of the compass
ante is Latin for before, giving the sense of prior

explanation.surface: An earlier person settled in lodgings in a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests lodgings but means compass points N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a city on the Loire in western France.

clue.text: Like list to include really good aggressive guy

parts.note: as means like, in the same way

indicators.note: to include means one word takes another inside it

parts.note: to list is to lean or slant, as a ship does
A1 means first-class, and in crosswords is written AI

explanation.surface: Something like a list that features something excellent and an aggressive man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' means lean, as a ship does, not a catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker who violently sets upon someone.

clue.text: An airman's control might make rail one rail

indicators.note: might make suggests these letters can be remade into something else

explanation.surface: A pilot's control mechanism could be formed from bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might make' rearranges RAIL ONE; the repeated 'rail' looks like a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft's wing used for banking and steering.

clue.text: Single lapse admitted by dope, a former entertainer

indicators.note: admitted by means taken inside the following word

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, also called dope
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
to err is to make a slip or lapse

explanation.surface: A one-time performer confessed a slip while on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: A pierrot was a white-faced clown in old seaside shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrots were costumed clowns in Victorian and Edwardian seaside concert parties.

clue.text: Disgusted expression about a head's cunning

indicators.note: about means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Someone says ugh at a headmaster's craftiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a school head but means a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is skill or subtle cleverness in handling a situation.

clue.text: Treated differently after a call for silence, so causing split

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the call for silence

parts.note: sh is the sound made to call for quiet

indicators.note: differently means the letters of treated are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Handled in a new way after someone hushed the room, causing division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges the word Treated, and 'after' puts that behind the hush; 'split' is the definition, not part of the instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattered means broken into fragments, much as split means broken apart.
